collection.title: 21 CFR Part 11 URS Requirements
collection.description: Structured user requirement examples mapped to current 21 CFR Part 11 references.

regulatorySource.title: 21 CFR Part 11 - Electronic Records; Electronic Signatures

content.statement: The system must be capable of detecting audit trail entries that have been altered since they were originally generated.
content.sourceStatement: The system must be capable of detecting any audit trails entries that have been altered since they were originally generated. (Only include this requirement if your system is capable of doing this.)
content.rationale: Supports validation of the system's ability to discern invalid or altered records.
content.applicability: Include only when the selected system can detect alteration of previously generated audit trail entries. If it cannot, assess alternative technical and procedural controls and document the resulting risk and supplier limitation.

content.statement: The system must restrict desktop administrative access to authorized administrator users.
content.sourceStatement: The system must restrict desktop access exclusively to admin users.
content.rationale: Limits privileged operating-system access that could bypass application controls or affect regulated records.
content.applicability: Apply when the computerized system includes a user-accessible desktop or operating-system layer. Define emergency, service, vendor, and break-glass access separately; this is an implementation example rather than verbatim wording from § 11.10(a).

content.statement: The system must be able to generate a batch record in PDF or CSV format.
content.sourceStatement: The system must be able to generate a batch record in PDF or CSV format.
content.rationale: Supports generation of accurate and complete record copies for inspection, review, and copying.
content.applicability: Apply only when the system creates or maintains batch records. Confirm that the chosen human-readable and electronic export formats preserve the complete record, context, metadata, and relationships; PDF or CSV may not be sufficient for every record type.

content.statement: The system must be able to generate audit trail exports in PDF or CSV format.
content.sourceStatement: The system must be able to generate audit trail exports in PDF or CSV format.
content.rationale: Makes audit trail information available for review, inspection, copying, and retention with the associated regulated records.
content.applicability: Apply where audit trails are required. Verify that exported data remain complete, readable, attributable, correctly ordered, and linked to the affected records; PDF or CSV may need supporting metadata or a native export.

content.statement: The system must provide a mechanism for periodic backups.
content.sourceStatement: There must be a mechanism in place to allow periodic system backups.
content.rationale: Supports protection, recovery, and ready retrieval of regulated records throughout their retention period.
content.applicability: Define backup scope, frequency, retention, security, monitoring, restoration testing, and recovery objectives from the intended use and risk assessment. A backup mechanism alone does not demonstrate recoverability.

content.statement: Applicable PCs and servers must be configured with RAID 1 mirroring.
content.sourceStatement: All PCs and Servers are to be configured in RAID 1 (mirroring).
content.rationale: Provides local storage redundancy against a single-disk failure where that architecture is selected.
content.applicability: Use only when RAID 1 is justified for the deployed architecture. RAID is not a backup and may not apply to cloud, managed, virtualized, appliance, or supplier-hosted systems; define equivalent resilience and recovery controls instead.

content.statement: Unused physical USB and Ethernet ports that are not necessary for system operation must be disabled or physically blocked.
content.sourceStatement: Unused physical ports (USB & Ethernet) not necessary for system operations must be disabled or physically blocked.
content.rationale: Reduces unauthorized access paths, uncontrolled data transfer, and connection of unapproved devices.
content.applicability: Apply to physical interfaces within the organization's control after assessing maintenance, support, emergency recovery, and approved peripheral needs. Define compensating controls when a port cannot be disabled or blocked.

content.statement: Servers must be located in lockable cabinets.
content.sourceStatement: All servers must be located in lockable cabinets.
content.rationale: Restricts unauthorized physical access to infrastructure that stores or processes regulated records.
content.applicability: Apply to on-premises servers when cabinet-level locking is part of the physical-security design. A controlled data room, managed data centre, cloud service, or sealed appliance may use different documented physical-access controls.

content.statement: The system must generate time-stamped audit trails that record applicable user actions and events, including user login, user logout, parameter changes, and alarm acknowledgement.
content.sourceStatement: The system must generate time-stamped audit trails that record user actions and events, including but not limited to the following: User log in; User log out; Parameter Changes; Alarm Acknowledged.
content.rationale: Provides independent, time-stamped evidence of relevant actions and changes affecting electronic records and system operation.
content.applicability: Define the event inventory from intended use and record risk. Part 11 specifically addresses entries and actions that create, modify, or delete electronic records; login, logout, parameter, and alarm events should be included when relevant to security, record context, or regulated decisions.

content.statement: The audit trail must identify the user who performed each applicable action or event, the date and time it occurred, and a description of the action or event.
content.sourceStatement: The audit trail must display the following at a minimum: Identify the user that performed each action or event (for user actions and events only); Date and Time when the action or event occurred; Description of action or event.
content.rationale: Provides the attribution, chronology, and event context needed to review regulated record history.
content.applicability: Apply to audit-trailed user actions and system events. Add old value, new value, reason for change, record identifier, electronic-signature meaning, or other context where the intended use and risk assessment require it.

content.statement: The system must ensure that new audit trail entries do not overwrite or modify existing entries.
content.sourceStatement: The system must be configured such that new audit trail entries will not overwrite or modify existing entries.
content.rationale: Preserves previously recorded information and the chronological integrity of the audit trail.
content.applicability: Apply wherever audit trails are used. Include retention, archival, capacity, purge permissions, database administration, and supplier-support paths in the assessment rather than testing only normal user functions.

content.statement: The system time must be synchronized with an approved authoritative time source, such as domain network time or an NTP server.
content.sourceStatement: The system time must be synchronized with the domain network time or NTP Server.
content.rationale: Supports consistent and reviewable timestamps across regulated records, audit trails, interfaces, and supporting infrastructure.
content.applicability: Select the authoritative source and permitted tolerance for the deployed architecture. Define monitoring, failure indication, time-zone handling, access to time settings, and recovery after disconnection.

content.statement: The system must display date and time in the format DD/MMM/YYYY and HH:MM.
content.sourceStatement: The time and date must be displayed in the following format: DD/MMM/YYYY & HH:MM.
content.rationale: Provides an unambiguous and consistently interpretable timestamp display for users and reviewers.
content.applicability: Treat this format as the book's example, not a verbatim Part 11 mandate. Select an unambiguous organization-approved format, define 12-hour or 24-hour time, seconds where needed, time zone, and exported-record behavior.

content.statement: The system must adjust for daylight saving time automatically.
content.sourceStatement: The system must be configured to adjust for daylight saving time automatically.
content.rationale: Supports consistent timestamp interpretation through seasonal clock changes.
content.applicability: Apply only where local time and daylight-saving rules are used. Systems standardized on UTC or deployed in regions without daylight-saving changes need different requirements; verify duplicate or skipped local times and time-zone metadata.

records.label: URS-P11-015
records.title: Enforce unique usernames
records.regulatoryLocator: §§ 11.10(d) and 11.10(g); see also § 11.300(a) for electronic signatures

content.statement: The system must enforce unique usernames by preventing duplicate usernames from being created.
content.sourceStatement: The system must enforce unique usernames by preventing duplicate usernames from being created.
content.rationale: Supports individual accountability, attributable actions, and reliable authority checks.
content.applicability: Apply to human user accounts. Define treatment of renamed users, reused identifiers, service accounts, federated identity, deleted accounts, and cross-site directories so historical attribution remains unambiguous.

content.statement: The system must require authentication with a unique username and password before allowing a user to log in.
content.sourceStatement: The system must require authentication with a unique username and password before allowing a user to log in.
content.rationale: Restricts system access and regulated operations to identified, authorized individuals.
content.applicability: Apply when username/password authentication is the approved mechanism. Federated identity, smart cards, passkeys, biometrics, or multifactor authentication require equivalent organization-approved requirements and must preserve individual attribution.

content.statement: The system must obscure passwords while they are being entered.
content.sourceStatement: The system must obscure passwords when they are being entered.
content.rationale: Reduces inadvertent disclosure of authentication secrets during interactive entry.
content.applicability: Apply to interfaces that accept passwords. If a temporary reveal control is provided, define its authorization, duration, logging, and shoulder-surfing risk; do not expose passwords in logs, exports, or error messages.

content.statement: The system must store passwords in a non-human-readable form, such as a suitably protected one-way hash.
content.sourceStatement: The system must store passwords in a non-human readable form (e.g., hashed).
content.rationale: Reduces the likelihood that stored authentication secrets can be recovered and misused.
content.applicability: Apply where the system stores password verifiers. Confirm current approved hashing, salting, work factors, key or pepper protection, migration, backup exposure, and supplier controls; encryption alone is not necessarily an equivalent password-storage design.

content.statement: The system must enforce passwords of at least eight characters containing uppercase letters, lowercase letters, numbers, and special characters.
content.sourceStatement: The system must enforce password complexity rules, including a minimum of 8 characters, a mixture of uppercase letters, lowercase letters, numbers, and special characters.
content.rationale: Implements the book's example control for reducing easily guessed passwords.
content.applicability: Treat the numeric and character-class rules as an example, not verbatim Part 11 text. Select current organization-approved authentication controls based on threat, system capability, identity-provider policy, password length, compromised-password screening, multifactor authentication, and user burden.

content.statement: The system must allow users to change their password securely.
content.sourceStatement: The system must allow users to change their password.
content.rationale: Allows a user to replace an expiring, exposed, or suspected-compromised credential without losing individual identity.
content.applicability: Apply to locally managed passwords. Define current-password verification, identity-provider ownership, session handling, notification, audit logging, and recovery when the system uses centralized or federated authentication.

content.statement: The system must prevent users from reusing any of their previous four passwords.
content.sourceStatement: The system must prevent users from reusing any of their previous four passwords.
content.rationale: Implements the book's example control for preventing immediate recycling of old credentials.
content.applicability: Treat four-password history as an organization-specific example. Align history depth with the approved identity policy, password-aging approach, compromise response, system capability, and centralized identity provider.

records.label: URS-P11-022
records.title: Lock accounts after failed logins
records.regulatoryLocator: § 11.10(g); see also § 11.300(d) for electronic-signature credential safeguards

content.statement: After an administratively configurable number of unsuccessful login attempts, the system must lock the account or prevent further login attempts for 30 minutes.
content.sourceStatement: After an administratively configurable number of unsuccessful login attempts, the system must lock out the user account or prevent them from attempting to log in again for 30 minutes.
content.rationale: Implements the book's example safeguard against repeated unauthorized credential attempts.
content.applicability: Treat the attempt count and 30-minute period as organization-specific values. Assess denial-of-service risk, progressive delay, administrative unlock, alerting, reporting, shared infrastructure, emergency access, and identity-provider controls.

content.statement: The system must force users to reauthenticate or log in again after an administratively configurable period of inactivity.
content.sourceStatement: The system must force users to re-authenticate/re-login after an administrative configurable period of inactivity.
content.rationale: Reduces the likelihood that an unattended authenticated session can be used by another individual.
content.applicability: Define the inactivity period from use environment, process duration, safety, availability, shared-terminal risk, electronic-signature workflow, and identity-provider capability. Consider screen locking separately from application-session termination.

content.statement: The system must provide a secure mechanism for a user to set a new password after forgetting the current password.
content.sourceStatement: The system must provide a secure mechanism for a user to set a new password if they forget their current password.
content.rationale: Restores authorized access while protecting the account from unauthorized reset and takeover.
content.applicability: Define identity proofing, reset authorization, token lifetime, single use, notification, audit logging, help-desk controls, temporary credentials, and federated identity ownership. Do not rely on knowledge available to unauthorized users.

content.statement: The system must force users to reset their password the first time they log in.
content.sourceStatement: Users must be forced to reset their password the first time they log in.
content.rationale: Prevents continued use of administrator-known, supplier-set, default, or temporary initial credentials.
content.applicability: Apply when temporary or initial passwords are issued. Federated identity, invitation links, passwordless onboarding, or user-created credentials require an equivalent mechanism that prevents shared or administrator-known secrets from remaining active.

content.statement: The system must allow an authorized administrator to remove or deactivate a user's access without removing the user's historical attribution.
content.sourceStatement: It must be possible to remove or deactivate a given user’s access.
content.rationale: Allows timely revocation of access while preserving the identity associated with historical records and actions.
content.applicability: Apply to locally managed or federated accounts. Define authorization, timing, session revocation, interfaces, disabled-account retention, rehiring/reactivation, service accounts, and evidence that deactivation propagated to all relevant components.

content.statement: The system must support user groups defined by an approved user-group access matrix, including Operator, Supervisor, Maintenance, and Administrator where applicable.
content.sourceStatement: The system must be configured with the following user groups as per a defined user group access matrix: Operator; Supervisor; Maintenance; Administrator.
content.rationale: Supports authority checks and segregation of permitted system operations by assigned role.
content.applicability: Treat the four role names as examples. Define roles from the actual process, segregation-of-duties needs, least privilege, supplier access, Quality oversight, emergency access, and approved access matrix; avoid broad default privileges.

records.label: URS-P11-028
records.title: Enforce data-entry limits
records.regulatoryLocator: § 11.10(h); related operational checks may also fall under § 11.10(f)

content.statement: The system must prevent data entry outside predefined approved limits.
content.sourceStatement: The system must prevent data entry outside of pre-defined limits.
content.rationale: Supports valid input and prevents values outside approved process, product, or data constraints from being accepted without control.
content.applicability: Apply only where justified limits exist. Define boundary behavior, units, precision, warning versus rejection, authorized overrides, reason capture, interface inputs, device checks, and change control for the limits.

content.statement: Electronically signed electronic records must contain the printed name of the signer, the date and time the signature was executed, and the meaning associated with the signature.
content.sourceStatement: Electronically signed electronic records must contain the following: The printed name of the signer; The date and time when the signature was executed; The meaning (such as review, approval, etc.) associated with the signature.
content.rationale: Makes the identity, execution time, and purpose of each electronic signature visible with the signed record.
content.applicability: Apply to every electronic record signed within Part 11 scope. Ensure the manifestation remains part of human-readable displays and copies, is linked to the signed record, and uses controlled signature meanings appropriate to the workflow.

content.statement: During a continuous period of controlled system access, the system must require all electronic-signature components for the first signing and at least one component executable only by the individual for each subsequent signing.
content.sourceStatement: When signing for an electronic signature while logged into a system, the system must prompt the user to re-enter their password at a minimum.
content.rationale: Implements the continuous-session electronic-signature component controls defined in § 11.200(a)(1)(i).
content.applicability: Apply to non-biometric electronic signatures during a single continuous controlled session. The normalized statement follows the current eCFR more closely than the book's password-only example; define how the system establishes and ends continuous controlled access.

content.statement: For a signing outside a single continuous period of controlled system access, the system must require all electronic-signature components for each signing.
content.sourceStatement: The system must require users to be logged in before they can execute electronic signatures. Once logged in, they must be prompted to re-enter their password at a minimum in order to execute electronic signatures.
content.rationale: Implements the non-continuous-session electronic-signature component controls defined in § 11.200(a)(1)(ii).
content.applicability: Apply to non-biometric electronic signatures not executed during one continuous controlled session. The normalized statement follows the current eCFR more closely than the book's login-plus-password example; verify all required signature components for each signing.

content.statement: After an administratively configurable period, the system must force users to change their password.
content.sourceStatement: After an administratively configurable period of time, the system must force users to change their password.
content.rationale: Implements the book's password-aging example for periodic review, recall, or revision of identification-code and password issuances.
content.applicability: Define the aging period from the approved identity policy, current security guidance, compromise-detection capability, multifactor authentication, system constraints, and § 11.300(b). Treat forced periodic change as an example, not the only possible implementation of periodic credential review or revision.
